data.title: Guangzhou R&F Discloses Major Litigation Over RMB473 Million Loan
data.description:
Guangzhou R&F Properties Co ( (HK:2777) ) has provided an announcement.

Guangzhou R&F Properties Co., Ltd. is a PRC-based joint stock property developer listed in Hong Kong under stock code 2777, and it has several outstanding corporate bond series traded in the domestic Chinese market. The group’s operations encompass real estate development and associated businesses, supported by a diversified capital structure that includes multiple onshore bond issues.

The company has reported a significant legal case initiated by a bank’s Guangzhou branch over a RMB473,550,000 loan involving its Huizhou subsidiary and related entities. The claimant seeks full repayment of principal, accrued interest and penalties, priority rights over mortgaged properties and pledged hotel income, and joint and several liability from Guangzhou R&F and another Huizhou developer, highlighting heightened legal and credit risk exposure for the issuer and its bondholders.

data.title: Fortior Technology Shareholders Approve 2026 A Share Restricted Incentive Scheme at EGM
data.description:
Fortior Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. Class H ( (HK:1304) ) has shared an announcement.

Fortior Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. held an extraordinary general meeting in Shenzhen on 14 September 2026, with all five directors in attendance and voting conducted through a combination of on-site and online methods compliant with PRC company law. Of the 115,114,080 issued shares, 78,078,891 were eligible to vote after certain major shareholders were required to abstain from specific resolutions under Hong Kong Listing Rules.

A total of 284 shareholders or proxies, representing about 20.58% of the voting share capital, participated in the meeting, including both A and H shareholders. Shareholders approved by poll a special resolution to adopt the 2026 A Share Restricted Share Incentive Scheme and to issue restricted shares under it, with strong support from A shareholders and majority backing from H shareholders, signaling endorsement of the company’s proposed equity-based compensation plan.

The company expects the prospective cooperation to potentially drive profit growth for both parties and strengthen its overall development trajectory, though it remains subject to due diligence and board approval.
